newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FNB SEES S.AFRICA RATES SIDEWAYS, THEN CUT.
newsitem.headline: FNB SEES S.AFRICA RATES SIDEWAYS, THEN CUT.

text.p: Banking group, First National Bank Holdings Ltd, said on Wednesday South African interest rates were seen sideways for a while, but was confident that the next move would be a reduction in the lending rate.
"Our official prognosis is that rates are going to go sideways for a while, but that we will get cuts...The current view is that we will get two cuts," said Viv Bartlett, FNB's managing director.

"If we see credit creation and inflation moving in the right way over the next couple of months, then we believe we will get a cut. And we believe that is going to happen," he told Reuters in an interview.
However, Bartlett said the bank had had to revise forecasts on the timing and size of a rate decrease.
"We do believe the next move is down but it is being deferred...Three or four months ago (we would have said) middle of the year and perhaps more cuts than the two."
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals last month snuffed out any lingering hopes of a near-term cut in interest rates, warning the next move could in fact be up.
Stals said that even more stringent measures might be needed to curb liquidity and excessive credit growth, leading to even higher interest rates.
South Africa's official central Bank rate is 17.0 percent and the prime lending rate 20.25 percent.
